What an SBA 7(a) acquisition loan requires, as of October 1, 2026.

The Small Business Administration rewrote its lending procedures for business acquisitions this year. These are the rules a buyer, a seller and their advisers meet on a 7(a) acquisition loan, taken from the procedure itself. Capital Row is not a lender and does not package or broker loans; this page is information, not advice.
The rules

sections.name: Ten rules a buyer and a seller meet on a 7(a) acquisition loan.

items.text: SBA acquisition loans · The rules
Ten rules a buyer and a seller meet on a 7(a) acquisition loan.
Maximum 7(a) loan

The most any one standard 7(a) loan can be. SBA guarantees 75 percent of loans above $150,000 and 85 percent at or below it, with a maximum guaranty of $3.75 million to one business and its affiliates.
Equity injection, initial acquisition

Measured on total project cost. For a first acquisition the injection cannot be reduced or eliminated. For a business expansion or an owner buyout the lender may reduce it where the borrower has sufficient liquidity and no negative net worth at the last year end.
Half
The most a seller note can count

Seller debt counts toward the equity injection only if it is subordinated and on full standby, with no payments of principal or interest for the term of the 7(a) loan, and only up to half of the required injection. Every other seller note is debt.
Independent valuation above

Where the business purchase price, real estate excluded, exceeds $350,000, or the buyer and seller are related, the lender must obtain a valuation from an accredited, independent valuator, prepared for the lender. A valuation prepared for the buyer or the seller may not be used.
Quality of earnings at or above

For an initial acquisition or a business expansion at a purchase price of $3 million or more, the lender must obtain a quality of earnings report with a cash proof, from an independent financial professional, for the lender. Owner buyouts and special purpose properties are exempt.
Debt service coverage

Historical earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, divided by all debt service after the transaction, using the last fiscal year or the average of the last two. Projections may not be used to meet it.
10 years
Maximum amortization
For the business, goodwill and working capital, with no balloon. Only the real estate portion may run longer, to 25 years, blended on a weighted average.
24 months
The seller may stay, as a consultant
In an initial acquisition the seller may not remain as an owner, officer, director or employee. A consulting role of up to 24 months is allowed. Seller earnouts are prohibited.
Owners must be U.S. citizens or nationals

From March 1, 2026, every direct and indirect owner and every required guarantor must be a U.S. citizen or national with a principal residence in the United States. Lawful permanent residents are no longer eligible.
Upfront guaranty fee, larger loans

For fiscal year 2027, on the guaranteed portion: 2 percent at or below $150,000; 3 percent to $700,000; above that, 3.5 percent on the first $1 million of the guaranteed portion and 3.75 percent on the rest. A $5 million loan at a 75 percent guaranty carries an upfront fee of $138,125.

items.text: SBA acquisition loans · What it means
What a seller can agree to, and who may be paid for a referral.
What a seller can and cannot agree to

A seller note that counts as the buyer’s equity is on full standby for the life of the loan: no principal and no interest until the SBA loan is repaid. Interest may accrue, and the note may amortize afterward.

A seller note that is not on standby is debt, and the total debt supporting the purchase, including that note, is limited to the valuation amount. If the price exceeds the valuation, the difference is made up with equity or standby funds.
The seller cannot take an earnout. Working capital true-ups are allowed.

The seller cannot remain in the business except as a consultant for up to 24 months. In a partial buyout, a selling owner who keeps under 20 percent must guarantee the loan for at least two years after disbursement.

The lender checks the seller’s financial data against IRS tax transcripts, and the quality of earnings report, where one is required, must reconcile the accountant-prepared statements, the tax returns, the internal statements and the transcripts.
Out-of-pocket costs of the valuation and the quality of earnings report may be passed to the borrower, and count toward the borrower’s equity injection.
What it means for a software or services acquisition

A buyer is treated as expanding, rather than acquiring for the first time, only if it has operated for two full fiscal years under its current ownership and the target is in the same four-digit industry group. Otherwise the deal is an initial acquisition: the 10 percent injection cannot be waived, debt service coverage must reach 1.25, and a quality of earnings report is required at $3 million. Intangible assets and goodwill, which are most of what a software company is, are financeable on a ten-year term. A virtual business may be confirmed without a physical site visit if the lender documents the alternative.
Who may be paid for a referral

SBA rules require anyone who refers an applicant to a lender, or a lender to an applicant, for a fee to disclose the fee on SBA Form 159, signed by the applicant, the agent and the lender. An agent may be paid by the applicant or by the lender, but not both for the same service. Fees must be reasonable and customary for the services actually performed, fees charged to the applicant may not be contingent on the loan being approved or closed, and a lender may not pass a referral fee to the borrower. In California, brokering commercial loans to a licensed finance lender requires a license under the California Financing Law; referrals to a bank are not within that definition, and a new law signed on September 30, 2026 will license commercial financing brokers for offers of $500,000 or less from July 1, 2028. Capital Row makes introductions through Capital Connections and does not package or broker loans; whether and how any introduction fee may be paid is a question of federal and state rules on which Capital Row takes counsel.
The procedure is public, it changed twice in sixteen months, and the lender reads the current one. So should the seller.
Our read

This page summarizes the procedure as published; the procedure governs. The rules differ for partial changes of ownership, employee stock ownership plans and special purpose properties, and SBA notices change them. A lender, an attorney and a CPA should confirm every item before it is relied on.
